technicalChanges.from: Python 2 compatibility remains available
technicalChanges.to: Python 3-compatible code is required
technicalChanges.implication: Apps, scripted inputs, custom commands, and templates that still use Python 2 syntax can stop working.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB 3.6 with the MMAP storage engine
technicalChanges.to: MongoDB 4.2 with the WiredTiger storage engine

technicalChanges.from: Legacy journal compression and tsidx writing defaults
technicalChanges.to: zstd journal compression and tsidx writing level 3 by default

technicalChanges.from: Deployment clients earlier than 7.0 can remain connected
technicalChanges.to: Version 7.0 or later is required with the hardened 9.0 deployment server
technicalChanges.implication: Older deployment clients can lose communication after the deployment-server security change.
technicalChanges.action: Identify clients earlier than 7.0, upgrade them, and review whether the deployment server must be isolated before upgrading.

requirements: Splunk Enterprise 9.0 moves KV Store from MongoDB 3.6 to 4.2. Complete the documented migration and validate apps that depend on KV Store.

technicalChanges.to: Libraries older than jQuery 3.5 are restricted by default
technicalChanges.implication: Classic dashboards and custom apps that depend on older jQuery behavior can fail unless remediated or temporarily re-enabled.
technicalChanges.action: Run the jQuery Upgrade Readiness checks and migrate app JavaScript to supported APIs.

technicalChanges.from: Event format inferred from the destination log name

technicalChanges.action: Review Windows Event Collector subscriptions and explicitly set the format where destination naming does not convey it.

technicalChanges.from: New installations commonly use the splunk account
technicalChanges.to: The installer creates a least-privileged splunkfwd account
technicalChanges.implication: File ownership, protected-log access, service control, and deployment automation can depend on the operating-system identity.
technicalChanges.action: Validate permissions and installation automation for new or rebuilt Linux forwarders.

technicalChanges.from: Older x86-64 processors may remain usable
technicalChanges.to: AVX, SSE4.2, and AES-NI support is required for the KV Store 7 baseline

technicalChanges.from: Admins can temporarily re-enable older jQuery libraries
technicalChanges.to: Older-library controls and the Internal Library Settings page are removed
technicalChanges.implication: The self-service compatibility escape hatch for older app and dashboard JavaScript is no longer available.
technicalChanges.action: Remediate apps and dashboards that use unsupported or hot-linked libraries before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: web.conf and restmap.conf are treated as externally controlled static files
technicalChanges.to: Splunk sidecars can update both files dynamically under system/local
technicalChanges.implication: Configuration-management tools that automatically revert these writes can trigger instability or restart loops.
technicalChanges.action: Allow Splunk-managed portions of these files to change asynchronously and test configuration-management reconciliation.

requirements: Hosts require AVX, SSE4.2, and AES-NI processor support. Verify every target hostâ€”not only a representative node.

technicalChanges.action: Use Splunk's dedicated FIPS-mode upgrade and migration procedure and validate every participating component.

technicalChanges.from: SSLv3 and TLS 1.0/1.1 remain supported
technicalChanges.to: Legacy protocols remain available but are deprecated and generate warnings
technicalChanges.implication: Existing endpoints may still connect, but the deployment is on a path toward mandatory TLS 1.2 or later.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory every Splunk-to-Splunk and integration endpoint and begin certificate and protocol modernization before 10.4.

technicalChanges.from: Python 3.9 handles platform and Splunk Web functions
technicalChanges.to: Splunk Web uses Python 3.13; splunkd keeps Python 3.9 by default with Python 3.13 opt-in
technicalChanges.implication: The Web runtime and the application-extension runtime no longer have one simple version label.
technicalChanges.action: Test Splunk Web integrations separately and use Splunk's Python compatibility guidance before opting splunkd extensions into 3.13.

technicalChanges.from: A deprecated Node.js runtime is bundled with Splunk Enterprise
technicalChanges.to: The bundled Node.js runtime is removed
technicalChanges.implication: Apps that assume Node.js is supplied by the platform will no longer run.
technicalChanges.action: Identify Node.js-dependent apps and redesign them or package a supported application-owned runtime.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise can start as root by default
technicalChanges.to: Running as root is blocked by default
technicalChanges.implication: Startup, file ownership, privileged ports, boot integration, and scripted administration can depend on the service identity.
technicalChanges.action: Move to a least-privileged service account and validate file access, ports, startup, and operational automation.

technicalChanges.from: Legacy Fishbucket database backend
technicalChanges.to: A more reliable checkpoint backend writes new file-monitoring state
technicalChanges.implication: The upgrade is automatic, but an unsupported downgrade can lose newer checkpoints and re-ingest data.
technicalChanges.action: No migration is required; preserve recovery planning and avoid treating a downgrade as a supported rollback.

technicalChanges.from: Older Linux distributions may host Edge Processor
technicalChanges.to: Security updates require a currently supported Linux distribution
technicalChanges.implication: Unsupported Edge Processor hosts can crash after the control plane upgrade and cause data loss.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade every affected management and Edge Processor host operating system before moving the control plane to 10.2.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.2
technicalChanges.to: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.4 current maintenance release; 10.4.3 remains the documented minimum
technicalChanges.implication: Splunk published 10.4.4 on September 29, 2026. Version 10.4.2 can block tcpout forwarding pipelines when acknowledgements are enabled on a receiving heavy forwarder or indexer; the 10.4.3-or-higher floor remains in effect.
technicalChanges.action: Target 10.4.4 for new upgrade work. Do not use 10.4.2; if rollout timing constrains the target, treat 10.4.3 as the minimum and validate acknowledged forwarding before production rollout.

technicalChanges.from: splunkd uses Python 3.9 by default with Python 3.13 opt-in; Splunk Web already uses Python 3.13
technicalChanges.to: Python 3.13 becomes the default interpreter with Python 3.9 available as a fallback
technicalChanges.implication: Private apps, custom search commands, REST endpoints, scripted or modular inputs, and packaged libraries can expose Python-version assumptions when the default changes.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory Python-dependent extensions, confirm supported app releases, and test representative workflows with the 3.13 default before production rollout.

technicalChanges.from: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated but available
technicalChanges.to: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 support is completely removed
technicalChanges.implication: Splunk component and integration connections using a legacy protocol can no longer negotiate successfully.
technicalChanges.action: Move every endpoint to TLS 1.2 or later and validate the complete trust path before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: SHA-1-signed certificates are deprecated
technicalChanges.to: SHA-1 certificate signatures are rejected; SHA-256 or stronger is required
technicalChanges.implication: Internal and external connections can fail even when the protocol version itself is acceptable.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory and reissue SHA-1-signed certificates, then validate trust chains and mutual-authentication paths.

technicalChanges.from: Install media retains older MongoDB engine binaries
technicalChanges.to: Unsupported MongoDB binaries are removed; engine 7 or later is required
technicalChanges.implication: A deployment still using an older KV Store engine cannot rely on the 10.4 package to perform that older transition.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade KV Store to MongoDB engine 7 or later and verify app collections before starting the 10.4 upgrade.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB 7 is the supported pre-upgrade KV Store baseline
technicalChanges.to: MongoDB 8.0, upgraded automatically from a supported 10.x path
technicalChanges.implication: MongoDB 4.x and 6.x cannot move directly to the 10.4 engine, so older deployments need a supported bridge release and a validated KV Store backup.
technicalChanges.action: Reach the documented MongoDB 7 floor before 10.4, retain a validated KV Store backup, and verify app collections after the automatic engine upgrade.

technicalChanges.from: Overlapping kvstore settings can be ignored in favor of sslConfig
technicalChanges.to: TLS settings in the kvstore stanza take precedence
technicalChanges.implication: Conflicting protocol settings can produce unexpected KV Store connection failures after the upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Compare both server.conf stanzas and remove unused or conflicting TLS settings before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise can run under an administrator-level account
technicalChanges.to: Local service or non-administrator domain accounts are required
technicalChanges.implication: The installer can reconfigure a local-system deployment or halt when a domain service account remains an administrator.
technicalChanges.action: Choose and validate the target service account, file permissions, service control, and domain policy before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: jQuery 2 compatibility artifacts can remain
technicalChanges.to: jQuery 2, related feature flags, and the quarantine framework are removed
technicalChanges.implication: Apps that hotlink jQuery 2 or depend on version-specific APIs no longer function.
technicalChanges.action: Run AppInspect, migrate classic dashboards where required, and move custom JavaScript to jQuery 3-compatible APIs.

requirements: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.4 is the current published maintenance release. Do not use 10.4.2 because tcpout with useACK=true can block forwarding pipelines; 10.4.3 remains the documented minimum if 10.4.4 cannot yet be adopted.

technicalChanges.from: The versioned page did not expose an explicit 10.6 upgrade-path table
technicalChanges.to: The published table names supported 10.6 paths from 9.4.x, 10.0.x, 10.2.x and 10.4.x
technicalChanges.implication: Enterprise and Heavy Forwarder planning can use the documented release-line edges, while exact maintenance, app, OS, topology and receiver checks remain separate.
technicalChanges.action: Use 10.0.x or 10.2.x as the first step from 9.4.x; 10.0.x, 10.2.x and 10.4.x can then move to 10.6.x as listed. Validate exact maintenance releases before execution.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB-backed KV Store
technicalChanges.to: Cohosted PostgreSQL KV Store begins in 10.6
technicalChanges.implication: Migration starts automatically after upgrade unless postponed beforehand. KV Store writes and dependent ES/ITSI functions are impaired during migration; ITSI 5.0.x and lower require postponement.
technicalChanges.action: Verify KV Store 7.0+, more than 50% free disk space, healthy cluster and parallel backup. For ITSI 5.0.x or lower, set postgresMigrateOnStartup=false before upgrade and verify every member.

technicalChanges.from: Earlier documentation differs on removal versus temporary enablement
technicalChanges.to: 10.6 disallows TLS 1.0/1.1 for inter-Splunk connections; no temporary override
technicalChanges.implication: Connections still requiring legacy TLS cannot be restored with the earlier temporary switch.
technicalChanges.action: Validate TLS 1.2 or 1.3 on each inter-Splunk connection before upgrading. The unresolved 10.4 timing conflict remains separate.

technicalChanges.from: Remote providers can run older Enterprise release lines
technicalChanges.to: Remote Splunk Enterprise providers must be 10.4 or later
technicalChanges.implication: A 10.6 search head cannot rely on older remote providers for a supported federated-search topology.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory every remote provider and upgrade any provider below 10.4 before moving the federated-search head to 10.6.

technicalChanges.from: Some public certificates include both serverAuth and clientAuth EKUs
technicalChanges.to: Public issuers are expected to stop issuing dual-use certificates by March 1, 2027
technicalChanges.implication: Using a server-only public certificate for mutual TLS or KV Store client authentication can cause service disruption after renewal.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory certificates by component. Keep Splunk Web certificates serverAuth-only and use a suitable private PKI or client-auth chain for mutual-TLS and KV Store component certificates.

technicalChanges.from: Three-segment release identifiers
technicalChanges.to: Four-segment release identifiers can be published
technicalChanges.implication: Strict parsers, deployment rules, CMDB fields, and comparison scripts can reject or misorder valid releases.
technicalChanges.action: Test version parsing and ordering in automation, deployment tooling, reports, and asset inventories.

technicalChanges.from: Supported custom visualizations in Classic dashboards
technicalChanges.to: Custom Visualizations support in Classic dashboards is deprecated
technicalChanges.implication: Existing dashboards are not described as removed in 10.6, but new investment increases future migration risk.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory affected Classic dashboards and plan supported replacements without treating deprecation as immediate removal.

approaches.title: Greenfield
approaches.fit: Best when historical data can remain behind or age out and the priority is a clean, no-outage cutover.
strengths: Easy to align to current best practices
approaches.tradeoff: Historical data is not copied, and load testing is limited before redirection.

approaches.title: Dual running
approaches.fit: Best when the target must be validated with real production load and data can be sent to both environments temporarily.
strengths: Historical access can age out naturally
approaches.tradeoff: Requires parallel capacity and usually creates the longest migration window.

approaches.title: Full migration
approaches.fit: Best when historical data must move and the on-premises environment has a firm retirement deadline.
approaches.tradeoff: Requires an outage sized to data volume and offers the least forgiving rollback path.

breakingChanges: Open every required data and integration path

technicalChanges.from: Earlier applicable private-runner browser and HTTP-test behavior
technicalChanges.to: Runner 1.44.0 uses Chrome and Chromium 151 with refreshed security and maintenance components; runner 1.39.0 restores NTLM authentication for HTTP tests
technicalChanges.implication: Browser execution or NTLM-authenticated HTTP tests can behave differently depending on the private-runner line deployed; the two published version notes must not be treated as one universal SaaS backend change.
technicalChanges.action: Identify the runner version used by each private location, validate critical journeys against its documented browser runtime, and retest NTLM HTTP tests where that 1.39.0 correction applies.

technicalChanges.from: Logs handled outside the new integrated Observability Logs experience
technicalChanges.to: A cloud-only logs experience backed by a Splunk Cloud stack, Unified Identity, centralized RBAC, data-level access control, and OpenTelemetry or Data Manager onboarding
technicalChanges.implication: Access and data visibility depend on the paired Splunk Cloud environment, identities, roles, data-level controls, and onboarding path; this is not a customer-managed log service or proof of availability on every stack.
technicalChanges.action: Confirm the eligible stack and organization pairing, map identities and data access, then validate the supported onboarding path and MELT workflow before adoption.

technicalChanges.component: Observability free-edition provisioning from Splunk Cloud
technicalChanges.from: Observability trial onboarding outside the documented Splunk Cloud self-service flow
technicalChanges.to: Splunk Cloud Platform 10.6 admin or sc_admin users can request a trial organization in the Discover app and enumerate paired indexes for OpenTelemetry-compliant logs
technicalChanges.implication: The release-note entry is scoped to a 10.6 Cloud environment and privileged roles. It does not establish a generally available 10.6 platform route, premium-app pairing, regional schedule, or entitlement in Version Compass.
technicalChanges.action: Verify the actual Cloud stack version, Discover app, role, pairing, region, entitlement, and trial availability before using this onboarding path.

technicalChanges.from: Legacy plural k8s.pod.labels.* attributes remain available while stable names are opt-in
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.161 emits stable singular k8s.pod.label.* names and disables the legacy names by default
technicalChanges.implication: Dashboards, detectors, MetricSets, routing, and exports that still query legacy Kubernetes label attributes can stop matching after a standalone Collector or chart upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Use Splunk's documented dual-emission feature-gate combination during migration, update dependent content to the stable names, then retire the legacy attributes deliberately.

technicalChanges.from: container, pod, and node CPU usage are read from kubelet UsageNanoCores
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.161 calculates CPU usage and utilization from the rate of cumulative cpu.time counters by default
technicalChanges.implication: The affected metrics are absent on the first scrape after startup and can shift alert or dashboard baselines compared with the kubelet-provided value.
technicalChanges.action: Compare representative CPU series and detector thresholds before rollout; temporarily disable receiver.kubeletstats.cpuUsageScrapeBased only when the prior calculation must be retained.

technicalChanges.from: Chart 0.160.0 packages Collector 0.160.1, Target Allocator 0.158.0, and Operator 0.122.1
technicalChanges.to: Chart 0.161.0 packages Collector 0.161.0, Target Allocator 0.159.0, and Operator 0.123.0
technicalChanges.implication: The supported chart now inherits Collector 0.161's stable Kubernetes attribute names and scrape-rate CPU behavior; chart users no longer remain on the earlier 0.160.1 Collector baseline.
technicalChanges.action: Treat the Helm update as a Collector 0.161 rollout, migrate dependent content, rebaseline CPU signals, and validate the updated allocator and operator in a representative cluster.

technicalChanges.from: featureGates.useLightPrometheusReceiver remains an available chart path
technicalChanges.to: The light-receiver gate is deprecated in chart 0.161.0 and scheduled for removal in a future release
technicalChanges.implication: Deployments that retain the light receiver need a planned transition before a later chart removes the feature gate.
technicalChanges.action: Set featureGates.useLightPrometheusReceiver=false in a test deployment, validate standard Prometheus receiver collection and resource use, then schedule production migration.

technicalChanges.from: The audit-log parser emits rpc.jsonrpc.error_code and rpc.jsonrpc.error_message
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.161 enables the feature gate that stops emitting the deprecated v1.38.0 RPC attributes
technicalChanges.implication: Content that filters or enriches Google Cloud audit logs with the retired attribute names can lose matches.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory queries and processors that use the legacy RPC fields, migrate them to the current semantic convention, or temporarily disable the documented feature gate during transition.

technicalChanges.from: server.address and server.port appear on db.server.top_query log records
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.161 removes the duplicate log attributes and emits them as resource attributes by default
technicalChanges.implication: Queries, transforms, or exports that address these values only as log-record attributes can stop resolving the monitored endpoint.
technicalChanges.action: Update affected content to read the resource attributes and remove reliance on the retired receiver.sqlserver.RemoveServerResourceAttribute feature gate.

technicalChanges.from: Custom components can still compile against the deprecated pkg/service ZapOptions API
technicalChanges.to: OpenTelemetry Collector 0.161 removes ZapOptions from the service package
technicalChanges.implication: The packaged Splunk distribution is not affected by customer configuration alone, but custom Collector builds or extensions using that API can fail to compile or initialize.
technicalChanges.action: Review custom Collector source dependencies before rebasing on 0.161 and migrate off ZapOptions where applicable.

technicalChanges.from: Custom injector configuration under /etc/splunk/zeroconfig with runtime-specific files
technicalChanges.to: Official OpenTelemetry injector configuration under /etc/opentelemetry/injector with a shared default_env.conf
technicalChanges.implication: Existing custom values are not migrated automatically. Runtime variables outside the documented OTEL_* and SPLUNK_* set are ignored by the shared file, and instrumented services must be restarted after the preload or configuration change.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory the legacy java.conf, node.conf, and dotnet.conf values, migrate supported variables before upgrading, move runtime-specific settings to each service environment, and plan the documented restart or reboot.

technicalChanges.from: Deprecated scripted_inputs receiver remains available
technicalChanges.to: scripted_inputs is removed; splunk_inputs is the replacement behind the enableTArunner feature gate
technicalChanges.implication: A Collector configuration that still declares scripted_inputs cannot preserve that collection path after the 0.160 upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Replace scripted_inputs with the documented splunk_inputs configuration, enable and validate the required feature gate, and test Linux or Windows scripts before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: deployment_name_from_replicaset can remain in k8sattributes configuration
technicalChanges.to: The option is removed and its presence causes a hard Collector startup failure
technicalChanges.implication: Helm values or generated configurations that retain the key can prevent the Collector from starting. Old-format k8sattributes internal metrics are also disabled by default in this line.
technicalChanges.action: Remove deployment_name_from_replicaset, validate the documented ReplicaSet-derived behavior, and migrate dashboards or alerts that rely on the old processor self-telemetry format.

technicalChanges.from: Hardcoded linux:varlog and linux:bash_history assignments in the packaged Linux configuration
technicalChanges.to: Filename-based Splunk TA-style assignments, including bash_history, syslog, linux_secure, linux_audit, and config_file
technicalChanges.implication: Saved searches, routing, field extraction, retention, and billing assumptions keyed to the earlier sourcetypes can change after the package upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Compare representative Linux events before and after the upgrade and update downstream content only after confirming the new sourcetype contract.

technicalChanges.from: PowerShell and shell installation or update without the new immutable-release attestation check
technicalChanges.to: Splunk OpenTelemetry .NET 1.16 verifies immutable release assets and requires GitHub CLI by default for the PowerShell commands and shell installer
technicalChanges.implication: Customer-managed .NET instrumentation installation or update can stop before deployment when GitHub CLI is unavailable; explicit skip options bypass the new verification rather than satisfying it.
technicalChanges.action: Install and authorize GitHub CLI in the deployment path, validate artifact-attestation verification in a representative host or image, and treat any decision to use the documented skip option as a security exception.

technicalChanges.from: Pre-stable OpenTelemetry HTTP and database semantic-convention attribute names
technicalChanges.to: Stable semantic conventions in Splunk OpenTelemetry Node.js 4.11.0
technicalChanges.implication: Detectors, dashboards, MetricSets, routing, and API consumers that query renamed HTTP or database attributes can lose matches when the agent changes.
technicalChanges.action: Diff the documented HTTP and database attribute migrations, update queries and rules, and validate dual-version traffic during the agent rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk OpenTelemetry Node.js 4.11.0 with the prior OpenTelemetry SDK and database instrumentation set
technicalChanges.to: Version 4.12.0 with OpenTelemetry 2.11.0 / instrumentation 0.222.0, Couchbase SDK 4.7+ coverage and vendored MySQL2 instrumentation
technicalChanges.implication: Database span coverage and dependency behavior can change, while installation now skips native-extension compilation when the release has no matching prebuilt binary.
technicalChanges.action: Validate representative Couchbase and MySQL2 spans, existing HTTP/database attributes, and installation logs on every supported architecture before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Java instrumentation 2.31.0/2.31.1 can fail to turn off CPU profiling through remote configuration
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.31.3 re-releases the 2.31.2 fix and repairs Docker image publishing
technicalChanges.implication: Deployments that rely on remote configuration need the corrected agent and matching image before treating the profiling-off control as effective.
technicalChanges.action: Roll out the 2.31.3 agent or image in a representative service and verify that remote configuration stops CPU profiling without changing unrelated telemetry.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk distribution defaults and customer settings are applied through environment-variable configuration
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 accepts standard OpenTelemetry declarative configuration through OTEL_CONFIG_FILE, avoids applying the distribution's environment-variable defaults when that file is set, and applies Splunk resource information and the distribution.splunk trace-response-header option
technicalChanges.implication: Configuration precedence changes when OTEL_CONFIG_FILE is present. Profiling and callgraphs remain environment-variable-only, so a file-only migration can omit intended Splunk behavior if those boundaries are not retained.
technicalChanges.action: Test the same service with the intended declarative file and environment variables, verify effective resources and trace-response-header behavior, and keep profiling and callgraph variables explicit until Splunk documents declarative equivalents.

technicalChanges.from: Generated distribution metadata advertises SPLUNK_OTEL_SYSTEM_METRICS_ENABLED even though the runtime does not read it
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 removes the unsupported variable from generated metadata; system metrics remain enabled through auto-instrumentation and can be disabled with OTEL_PYTHON_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=system_metrics
technicalChanges.implication: Deployments that set the obsolete variable never controlled runtime system metrics, so retaining it can create a false belief that collection is disabled.
technicalChanges.action: Remove the ineffective setting from templates and use the documented disabled-instrumentations value when system metrics must be turned off; no runtime behavior change is implied by the metadata correction itself.

technicalChanges.from: Published Python init images target AMD64
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 publishes AMD64 and ARM64 variants for both standard and SecureApp init images
technicalChanges.implication: ARM64 Kubernetes workloads can use a matching init image instead of relying on an incompatible architecture, while standard and SecureApp images remain distinct deployment choices.
technicalChanges.action: Select the exact standard or SecureApp image for the workload, pin the intended 2.13.0 tag or digest, and validate injection and startup on representative ARM64 nodes before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: The distribution permits wrapt 2.2.2 or later
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 requires wrapt 2.5.0 or later
technicalChanges.implication: Application lock files, constraints, or base images pinned below wrapt 2.5.0 can conflict with installation or produce a different resolved environment during the agent upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Resolve the 2.13.0 agent in the application's locked dependency set, rebuild the deployment artifact, and run instrumentation smoke tests before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Rage clicks enabled by default, a five-second page-completion quiet window, and 2 MB localStorage retry persistence
technicalChanges.to: Four frustration signals enabled, a one-second quiet window, and up to 100 MB IndexedDB persistence for failed Session Replay uploads
technicalChanges.implication: Interaction volume, Page Completion Time baselines, client storage, privacy review, and replay retry behavior can differ without an application-code change.
technicalChanges.action: Review consent and storage policy, compare Page Completion Time baselines, and explicitly retain or disable earlier behaviors where the application requires them.

technicalChanges.from: spaMetrics is the configuration name used for single-page application navigation and page-completion settings
technicalChanges.to: Browser RUM 3.2 renames the configuration to navigationMetrics; spaMetrics remains supported as a deprecated alias
technicalChanges.implication: Existing deployments continue to work, but leaving the alias in templates or generated configuration creates future removal debt and can obscure where new manual page-load and blocking-element settings belong.
technicalChanges.action: Use navigationMetrics in new configuration, migrate maintained templates from spaMetrics during the normal rollout, and validate manual page-load registrations against the default 180-second maximum wait when adopted.

requirements: Splunk directs customers to contact their Splunk team for access to the Agent Observability SaaS deployment. Treat it as availability-bound, not universally enabled.
Use a custom role only for the non-admin users who should manage business transaction and endpoint rules, and validate create, update, and delete behavior under normal change controls.
Confirm Observability Logs pairing and access

Observability Logs is cloud-only and uses a Splunk Cloud stack, Unified Identity, centralized RBAC, data-level access control, and a supported OpenTelemetry or Data Manager onboarding path. Confirm each boundary before adoption.
Validate the applicable Synthetics private-runner line
Review private locations individually: runner 1.44.0 updates Chrome and Chromium to 151 and refreshes runtime components, while 1.39.0 restores NTLM authentication for HTTP tests.
Treat Cloud 10.6 trial onboarding as stack-specific

The documented free-edition flow requires Splunk Cloud Platform 10.6, the Discover Splunk Observability Cloud app, and an admin or sc_admin role. The current service pairing is now 10.6, but confirm stack, region, entitlement, schedule, pairing, and trial availability rather than inferring them from the platform line alone.

Detector Optimization is Controlled Availability. Confirm realm and access with Splunk, review each recommendation and its expected impact, and keep change approval with the customer because recommendations are not applied automatically.
Migrate Kubernetes semantic conventions for Collector and chart 0.161

Standalone Collector 0.161 and Kubernetes chart 0.161.0 use stable singular label and annotation attributes plus container.image.tags. Migrate dashboards, detectors, MetricSets, routing, and exports before rollout.
Rebaseline kubelet CPU metrics for Collector and chart 0.161
CPU usage and derived utilization now come from cpu.time rates by default and are absent on the first scrape after startup. Validate series behavior and thresholds before production rollout.
Move SQL Server endpoint lookups to resource attributes
Collector 0.161 removes server.address and server.port from db.server.top_query log attributes and makes them resource attributes by default.
Treat chart 0.161.0 as a Collector 0.161 upgrade

The Kubernetes chart published September 21, 2026 packages Collector 0.161.0 and its breaking Kubernetes semantic-convention and CPU-calculation defaults. Rehearse the Collector changes instead of treating the Helm update as an isolated chart change.
Plan migration to the standard Prometheus receiver
Chart 0.161.0 deprecates featureGates.useLightPrometheusReceiver. Validate the standard receiver with the gate set to false before a future chart removes the light-receiver path.
Validate the updated chart control plane
Chart 0.161.0 updates Target Allocator to 0.159.0 and Operator to 0.123.0. Validate allocation, reconciliation, and operator-managed instrumentation behavior in a representative cluster.
The 0.160 line replaces the custom injector shim and does not automatically migrate existing values into the new configuration files.
Collector 0.160 removes scripted_inputs. Convert to the splunk_inputs receiver and validate the required enableTArunner feature gate before production.
Remove the retired Kubernetes processor option
Any k8sattributes configuration that still includes deployment_name_from_replicaset fails hard at startup in Collector 0.160.
Provide GitHub CLI for .NET 1.16 installer verification

Splunk OpenTelemetry .NET 1.16 requires GitHub CLI by default when its PowerShell installation/update commands or shell installer verify immutable release attestations. Validate the tool and network path before rollout; skipping verification is an explicit exception, not the default readiness path.
Splunk OpenTelemetry Node.js 4.11.0 adopts stable OpenTelemetry HTTP and database semantic conventions with renamed attributes.

Splunk OpenTelemetry Node.js 4.12.0 upgrades the OpenTelemetry SDK and instrumentation packages, adds Couchbase SDK 4.7+ coverage, vendors MySQL2 instrumentation, and skips native compilation when no prebuilt binary is available. Validate span shape and installation behavior before broad rollout.

Java instrumentation 2.31.3 re-releases the 2.31.2 CPU-profiling remote-configuration fix and corrects Docker image publishing. Validate the profiling-off control against the exact agent or image deployed.

When OTEL_CONFIG_FILE is set, Splunk OpenTelemetry Python 2.13.0 does not apply the distribution's environment-variable defaults. Verify the declarative file, Splunk resource information and trace-response-header setting while retaining explicit environment variables for profiling and callgraphs.
Rebuild Python 2.13 dependency and image baselines

Python instrumentation 2.13.0 raises the wrapt minimum to 2.5.0 and publishes standard and SecureApp init images for ARM64. Resolve locked dependencies and validate the exact architecture-specific image before rollout.

Browser RUM 3.1 changes frustration-signal collection, Page Completion Time quiet-window behavior, and failed-replay storage defaults. Confirm privacy, storage, and detector assumptions before broad rollout.
Adopt the Browser RUM 3.2 navigationMetrics name

Browser RUM 3.2 keeps spaMetrics working as a deprecated alias, so no mandatory code or configuration change is required for this release. Use navigationMetrics for new configuration and migrate maintained templates before a future removal.

capabilities.desc: Builds and explains playbooks. Both editions, Cloud only; ES 8.6+ and paired SOAR Cloud. The task guide additionally requires Cloud Platform 10.1+ and a Splunk user account, and excludes FedRAMP SOAR stacks. ES 8.7 improves context handling.

notes.title: Cloud Connect and on-premises scope
notes.text: Detection Studio and TIM use Cloud Connect for on-premises access. The editions overview lists the ES AI Assistant through Cloud Connect under Premier. Cloud Connect supports private cloud and on-premises deployments; it does not turn Cloud-only agents into on-premises features.
notes.details: The guide requires access to *api.scs.splunk.com:443 and *auth.scs.splunk.com:443, or proxy configuration. Proxy settings affect the whole platform. Full access requires cloud_connection_product_get, license_read and license_edit; the first two allow read-only connection status.

notes.title: Edition inclusion is only one requirement
notes.text: Regional availability and ESâ€“SOAR pairing must be checked separately. A Cloud listing does not establish availability on every stack, cloud provider or regulated deployment.
notes.details: Splunk publishes distinct SOAR pairing matrices for Premier and other paired deployments. Pairing is unsupported on Enterprise 9.4.0â€“9.4.2. Review the source for exact SOAR versions, hybrid certificate requirements and government-cloud exclusions.

notes.title: Keep the two AI assistants distinct
notes.text: The ES AI Assistant is governed by ES edition scope. Splunk AI Assistant is a separately versioned platform app; its 2.1.0 notes support Agent Mode for Cloud Connected Enterprise customers in eligible AWS regions.
notes.details: The original comparison applied an old 1.1.0 on-premises restriction to the whole platform-app release history. That restriction is not a current blanket rule.

notes.title: Licensing and trial terms
notes.text: ES is used with Splunk Enterprise or Cloud Platform and does not add ingestion capacity. The 8.6 licensing guide documents 30-day Essentials and 90-day Premier trials.
notes.details: Existing Essentials customers trialing Premier revert to their purchased Essentials entitlement with retained access to Essentials features and processed data. Other trial expiry restrictions can block Mission Control, Detection Editor and Content Management; Premier trials also restrict UEBA. Confirm the applicable trial and contract terms.

notes.title: Public pricing models
notes.text: The current ES pricing section lists activity-based, workload and ingest options. The detailed activity-based FAQ identifies Splunk Cloud Platform, leaving ES deployment eligibility unclear. Standalone SOAR remains offered, but this page no longer specifies a seat-pricing model.
notes.details: Confirm product, deployment and contract eligibility with Splunk; do not infer universal activity-based pricing or a change to existing SOAR contracts. A quote or standalone license does not establish supported pairing or agent entitlement.

notes.title: Announcements and shipped releases
notes.text: The September Agentic SOC announcement describes expanded workflows and Exposure Analytics. Release-specific availability still comes from the product documentation.
notes.details: Keep marketing announcements, release features, regional delivery and customer enablement separate. Workflow groupings are explanatory, not an entitlement matrix.

claims.text: The current Enterprise Security pricing section lists activity-based, workload and ingest options.

conflicts.question: Confirm ES product, Cloud versus customer-managed deployment, and contract eligibility with Splunk.

conflicts.question: Ask Splunk to confirm Essentials entitlement and eligibility for the target deployment.

conflicts.title: Does the 8.7 label change Guided Response entitlement?

The 8.7 Cloud matrix places Triage and Guided Response enhancements in the Premier column.

conflicts.meaning: An enhancement grouping does not establish that the underlying feature became Premier-only. The sources cover different versions and scopes; 8.7 Essentials applicability remains unresolved.
conflicts.question: Ask which 8.7 Guided Response capabilities are available in Essentials, and which enhancements require Premier.

workflows.title: Build and maintain detections
workflows.text: Detection Studio manages detection content; Detection Builder assists authoring and troubleshooting. Automation Builder works with playbooks, while Connector Builder generates and refines integrations. The latter has an unresolved edition conflict.

workflows.title: Investigate and respond
workflows.text: Triage helps assess incoming findings; Guided Response helps run SOAR actions. AI SOC Analyst uses investigation and response-plan context. Check each agentâ€™s edition and pairing requirements before treating this as an available end-to-end workflow.

workflows.title: Understand suspicious activity
workflows.text: Premier adds native UEBA for behavioral analysis and Automated Threat Analysis powered by Attack Analyzer. Its Malware Reversing and Phishing Agent summarizes suspicious scripts; that agent is Cloud only and requires paired SOAR.

workflows.title: Bring context and procedures together
workflows.text: TIM supplies threat intelligence, Exposure Analytics adds entity and business context, and the SOP Agent converts an existing procedure into a response plan. The SOP Agent needs the ES assistant and response-template permissions.

highlights.title: Agent authoring and response
highlights.text: 8.7 introduces AI SOC Analyst and Connector Builder. Version 8.7.1 turns Connector Builder on for eligible users; AI SOC Analyst still requires Splunk enablement. Automation Builder improves context handling; Detection Builder improves SPL guidance. Connector Builderâ€™s edition scope remains disputed.

highlights.title: Investigation context and navigation
highlights.text: Security MCP tools expose investigation context. Navigation gains customization and preview; View Change History opens fuller analyst-change context through Activity Log searches.

highlights.title: Cloud matrix additions
highlights.text: The 8.7 matrix records Triage and Guided Response enhancements, automation-authoring changes and UEBA data-source and Entity Analysis performance improvements in Premier. Agent-level scope still needs the qualifications below.
